definitions: A literary movement that emerged in the 1950s, characterized by a rejection of traditional poetic forms and a focus on themes of existentialism, spirituality, and social nonconformity.
Poetry written by members of the the Beat Generation, often improvisational and free-verse, exploring themes of drug use, sexuality, and Eastern mysticism.
examples: Allen Ginsberg was a key figure in beat poetry.
The coffeehouse hosted a night of beat poetry.
She studied the history of beat poetry in college.
